instructions: At least 2 hours ahead, or the night before: squeeze the orange and 2 of the limes. That should be about 1/3 cup orange juice and 3 tbsp lime juice. Mince the 3 garlic cloves. In a large zip top bag, mix the juices and garlic with the 3/4 tsp cumin, the 3/4 tsp coriander, the 1 tsp smoked paprika, the 1/2 tsp chipotle powder, 3/4 tsp of the salt and 1/4 tsp of the pepper.

Cut the steak into 3 or 4 pieces that will fit in your skillet. Add them to the bag, press out the air, seal it and squish the marinade all over the meat. Refrigerate it for at least 2 hours, or overnight.

About 30 minutes before you cook, take the steak out of the fridge. Meanwhile, seed the 3 bell peppers and slice them into strips about 1/2 inch wide. Halve the onion and slice it about 1/4 inch thick.
Lift the steak out of the bag and throw away the marinade. Pat the pieces very dry with paper towels and rub them all over with 1 tbsp of the oil.

Heat a large cast iron skillet over high until it just starts to smoke. Add half the steak and leave it alone for about 2 minutes, until the underside is dark brown. Flip it and cook the other side for 1 1/2 to 2 minutes. Stand back a little. It'll spatter.

You're cooking the steak to 130°F in the middle for medium rare, so if you have a thermometer, check the thickest piece. No thermometer? Cut a small slit in the thickest part: it should be pink in the middle. Move it to a plate, cover it loosely with foil and cook the rest of the steak the same way.

Keep the skillet on high and add 1 tbsp of the oil. Add the onion, sprinkle it with 1/4 tsp of the salt and cook for about 5 minutes, stirring now and then, until it's soft with charred edges. Transfer it to a platter.

Add the last 1 tbsp oil and the bell peppers. Sprinkle them with the remaining 1/4 tsp salt and 1/4 tsp pepper. Cook for 5 to 6 minutes, stirring every minute or so, until they're charred in spots but still have a little bite. Add them to the platter.
While the peppers cook, wrap the 12 tortillas in a damp paper towel and microwave them for 45 seconds to 1 minute, until they're warm and soft. Keep them wrapped in a clean kitchen towel.
Look for the lines running along the steak and slice it thin across them. Pile it on the platter with any juices from the plate.
Slice the 2 avocados, chop a handful of the cilantro and cut the last lime into wedges. Slice the jalapeño thin for anyone who wants heat.
Taste a slice of steak. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt or a squeeze of lime.
Serve with the warm tortillas, avocado, sour cream, cilantro, lime wedges and jalapeño.
advance_prep_notes: marinate the steak at least 2 hours, or the night before
method_notes: Both season skirt or flank steak with lime, garlic, cumin, coriander and chipotle, sear it hard in a very hot skillet, rest it and slice it across the grain, and char peppers and onion in the same pan. RecipeTin Eats, the lead, marinates the steak in orange and lime juice for 2 hours to overnight, dries it, sears it about 1 1/2 minutes a side and cooks the onion and peppers separately until charred. Well Plated rubs the steak with spices and lime zest, adds Worcestershire and honey to a shorter marinade, and slowly caramelizes the vegetables with more spice. This follows the lead's marinade scaled to 1 1/2 lb for 4, using the lead's own smoked paprika swap for half the chipotle to keep it mild, with jalapeño at the table.
